checked_classes: Build-versus-adopt blind spots — The artifact compares the existing UAR runtime with a timing library, a durable job library, and a workflow platform. It distinguishes library-provided timing from UAR-owned authority and transactional guarantees, records maintenance evidence for external candidates, and requires an exact-version fit gate before scheduler adoption.

Unevaluated candidates — All seven candidates have explicit verdicts, evidence, risks, and decision rationales. Reference-only alternatives are distinguished from conditional adaptation recommendations.

Stale or unverifiable landscape claims and missing solution categories — The comparison covers timing adapters, persistent job queues, workflow orchestration, and existing domain infrastructure. Tagged scheduler and Apalis documentation and registry endpoints support the stated landscape; main-branch evidence is explicitly bounded, the stale Temporal preview description is excluded, and unresolved licensing is disclosed rather than treated as settled.

Contradictions with assessment, goals, or constraints — The dependency-pin warning in the assessment handoff is addressed through explicit effective-input tracing without approving policy divergence. Runtime findings remain source-level and unreproduced, publication is separated from deployment health, reliability foundations precede unattended features, and OpenSpec deltas remain required for Plan. The packet supplies no additional project constraints.
